documents.title: Primary care: abnormal liver tests
documents.text: 17-year-old with ALT 96 U/L found on sports physical. No alcohol use. Hepatitis B and C serologies negative. Repeat in three months.

documents.title: Repeat liver panel
documents.text: ALT 88 U/L, AST 71 U/L. Bilirubin normal. Albumin normal.

documents.title: Liver ultrasound
documents.text: Mildly echogenic liver suggestive of fatty infiltration. Spleen upper normal size. No focal lesion.

documents.title: Hepatology: elevated transaminases
documents.text: Persistent transaminase elevation with fatty-appearing liver. BMI 22. Ceruloplasmin 22 mg/dL, within reference range, so Wilson disease considered unlikely. Working diagnosis: nonalcoholic fatty liver disease.

documents.title: Psychiatry: mood changes
documents.text: New irritability, low mood, and declining university grades over six months. Diagnosis: depressive episode. Started sertraline.

documents.title: Primary care: hand tremor
documents.text: Fine tremor in both hands, worse when writing. Attributed to sertraline. Dose reduced.

documents.title: Neurology: tremor and speech
documents.text: Tremor persists after stopping sertraline. Mild slurring of speech noted by family. Brain MRI ordered. Bedside eye exam without slit lamp shows no obvious corneal ring.

documents.title: Brain MRI
documents.text: Symmetric T2 hyperintensity in the bilateral putamen and thalami. Differential includes metabolic and toxic causes. Clinical correlation recommended.

documents.title: Liver panel and blood count
documents.text: ALT 74 U/L. Platelets 128 x10^9/L. Hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL with elevated reticulocyte count.

documents.title: Primary care: follow-up
documents.text: Patient asks whether the brain MRI findings were ever explained. No 24-hour urine copper or slit lamp exam is documented. Brother had unexplained liver disease as a teenager per patient.
